core_obligations: Introduce the closed subscheme X times Y of affine 2n-space with coordinates x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_n and identify X cap Y with the intersection of X times Y with V(x_1 - y_1, ..., x_n - y_n) (proof lines 6347-6349).
For a closed point t of the intersection, use the dimension formula for products to get dim_t(X times Y) = dim(X) + dim(Y) = r + s, hence dim(O_{X times Y, t}) = r + s (proof lines 6350-6354).
Apply the one-equation dimension lemma to the quotient by the n linear forms and obtain dim(O_{X cap Y, t}) >= r + s - n (proof lines 6355-6360).
Translate the pointwise dimension bound into the statement about the dimension of every irreducible component of X cap Y (proof lines 6361-6362).
proof_roadmap: Embed the intersection in the product with the diagonal linear subspace.
Compute the local dimension of the product.
Apply the one-equation bound n times.
Convert the local bound into a component statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the expected dimension bound for the intersection of an r-dimensional and an s-dimensional equidimensional closed subset of affine n-space. The proof introduces the product X times Y inside affine 2n-space with coordinates x_i and y_i, realizes X cap Y as the intersection of the product with the linear subspace V(x_1 - y_1, ..., x_n - y_n), and at a closed point t of the intersection computes dim(O_{X times Y, t}) = r + s using the dimension of a product together with the local dimension lemma (proof lines 6347-6354). The one-equation dimension lemma over a local ring then gives dim(O_{X cap Y, t}) >= r + s - n, and the local dimension lemma converts this into the statement about irreducible components (proof lines 6355-6362). H2: the product trick and the two dimension comparisons are the substance.
